items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: "the same thing I think applied to Darnier all of them which is a strange state of affairs"

ctx.x: well this is one of the aspects of criticism that gives a critic confidence if he finds enough agreement in his peers he he says I belong as a critic and the musicians themselves were I think as critical as anybody

the funny I would say that of those musicians as well let's take Bix as an example he made probably 110 odd records I don't think that any of us would ever say that Bix ever played a bad note I'm not saying he didn't miss one because of his lip or something but never one where it was in a taste that we'd question and the same thing I think applied to Darnier all of them which is a strange state of affairs
if they acquired good status it was because they knew the right notes it was because intuitively they had
